text:
[LERR.8.2] **The bands are normative, and an enum cannot express them.**
This is the residue English has to carry.

| Range | Category |
|---|---|
| `0` | success |
| `-1..-99` | generic |
| `-100..-199` | input: a fact, a text or an encoded body that does not fit |
| `-200..-299` | runtime |
| `-300..-399` | reserved, out of use |
| `-400..-499` | storage and integrator callbacks |
| `-500..-549` | artefact load — the container, then its atoms      |
| `-550..-599` | AOT code load |
| `-600..-699` | native Rete loader, realtime, series-backend ABI |
| `-700..-799` | dialect binding, realtime contract, event trace |
| `-800..-9999` | reserved for future categories |
| `-10000` and below | integrator-defined; an implementation never returns one |

Zero is success, negatives are errors, positives are unused.

**A new code must fit its band's theme**, and a new *category* claims a
range by amending the register ([IERR.2.8.1]) before allocating in it: an allocation nobody
recorded is one nobody can see colliding.

The band a code sits in is therefore part of what it means. Two codes with
adjacent numbers in different bands are less related than two with distant
numbers in the same one, and a caller may reasonably branch on the range
alone — a `-5xx` says *this artefact will not load* whatever the specific
value.
